rules.summary: Remove repeated transitions where the connection is already clear.
State the fact without announcing its importance.

Check whether these repeated opening transitions add information.
Replace the generic opening with the document's subject.
Replace repeated section announcements with their subject.
Check whether each hedge expresses a distinct uncertainty; retain needed qualifications.
Check whether these intensifiers add a measurable distinction.
Consider a shorter phrase that preserves the condition or meaning.
Em dashes exceed the selected local density; punctuation can be intentional.
Several short lists fragment this section; check whether the grouping helps readers.
Check whether this guarantee has conditions or exceptions.
Replace clustered stock metaphors with specific properties.
Replace the cluster of evaluative modifiers with specific properties.
Replace general praise with a specific property or measured result.
Remove a phrase forbidden by this editorial policy.
The ARI formula exceeds the selected level; consider the audience and keep necessary technical terms.
Consider paragraph boundaries while keeping each condition with the statement it qualifies.
This sentence is repeated; consider whether every occurrence is needed.
The first paragraph closely echoes its heading; check whether it adds information.
These sentences have high lexical overlap; check for repeated information.
This phrase recurs in a short prose window; check whether each use is needed.
Several paragraphs repeat the same opening formula.
These prose blocks have high lexical overlap; check for repeated information.
Several sentences repeat the same opening; consider removing repeated setup.
This summary has high lexical overlap with preceding prose; check what it adds.

Start with the subject instead of a conversational acknowledgment.
Start with the subject instead of announcing the explanation.

Consider a direct verb while preserving the subject, conditions, and technical meaning.
